# Loaders and progress

<!-- Generated by `python3 scripts/pick.py --write-docs references` from assets/library/techniques.json. Edit the JSON, then regenerate. -->

Loaders, step lists and progress that read as work being done, timed to resolve on a beat. 17 entries, by category and role. The [index](../technique-library.md) lists every family and each category's house rule.

### Bubble charges with colour, then snaps wide

`dv-charge-and-snap` · transitions · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

A typing pill fills with the accent on an expo-in while its dots fade and its width creeps, then snaps wide in one frame into a bar that eases to its final width.

- **Build:** MorphChain with a one-frame CHAIN_STEP after a fill window. Anatomy: Fill expo-in 28 f; width creep 185 -> 223 px; snap to 466 px in 1 f; ease 13 f. Sound: None needed; a soft hit on the snap.
- **Primitive:** `fx/MorphChain`
- **Timing:** 44 f in all.
- **Use when:** The answer arriving after a typing indicator.
- **Avoid when:** Snapping without the charge.

### Agent step list: spinner rows that tick to checks

`dv-agent-step-list` · ui choreography · workhorse · energy medium · any

The product shows its work as a list of steps: each row starts with a small spinner (a dashed ring or an arc) and its words step in at partial ink, then the line fades up and the spinner turns into a check; rows cut on with a coloured verb that drains to ink as the next row arrives; the list jumps up a row (or half a row) unanimated, or pushes up in 3-frame expo steps; the cadence of rows shortens toward the end (9, 9, 7, 5, 4, 3, 3 f).

- **Build:** Build: <StepList rows={stepCadence(start, n).map((at) => ({ at }))} labels x y width font colors> (fx/Loaders): rows cut on with a spinner (120 deg per 3 f at 30 fps) and the verb in the accent at 45 % ink, the line fades up (14 f), the spinner swaps to a check (3 f) and the verb drains to ink as the next row arrives (6 f); the list jumps a row unanimated past window (or jump="expo"); house cadence 18, 18, 14, 10, 8, 6, 6 f. Anatomy: Row = spinner + verb (accent tint) + grey detail + optional right icon; thin thread line on the left; status line eases down 12 px before a new row (anticipation); list jump 93-94 px in one frame. Sound: Rows within 60 ms of wood-block or drum hits; dings on rows; a glockenspiel on the last. Materials: Each step's icon draws itself: a short arc grows clockwise to about 270 deg and closes into a circle (12 f), the check draws in 4 f; icon 16 px, stroke 1.5 px in the row's current colour; the row text walks through a short hue path to ink as it completes (28-44 f), or each verb takes its own pastel tint and slides in 10 px over 16 f before cooling to white; a 2 px guide line pre-draws down the left 12 f before the first row; pending steps stay a dashed ring of 8 dashes.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Loaders.StepList`
- **Materials:** Each step's icon draws itself: a short arc grows clockwise to about 270 deg and closes into a circle (12 f), the check draws in 4 f; icon 16 px, stroke 1.5 px in the row's current colour; the row text walks through a short hue path to ink as it completes (28-44 f), or each verb takes its own pastel tint and slides in 10 px over 16 f before cooling to white; a 2 px guide line pre-draws down the left 12 f before the first row; pending steps stay a dashed ring of 8 dashes.
- **Timing:** Rows every 14-50 f (shortening); spinner about 120 deg per 3 f; check swap 2-4 f; line fade 12-16 f; verb drain 4-6 f.
- **Use when:** AI agents, builds, workflows, any "it is doing it" moment.
- **Avoid when:** Smooth scrolling lists (the steps should feel like software); more than about seven rows.

### Progress spine leads the steps

`ui-progress-spine-steps` · ui choreography · workhorse · energy calm · feature, walkthrough, launch, vertical

A thin line grows down the side of a step list with a dot at its head. Each step appears as the head reaches it, works with a spinner and a typed detail line, then flips to done, and the list scrolls to keep the head in view until the line turns a rounded corner toward the result.

- **Build:** Build the spine as one SVG path: a vertical run down the list's left gutter, then optionally a 40 px-radius arc into a horizontal run toward the result card. Place the head, a flat 10 px dot in C.ink, at getPointAtLength(L(f)) (from @remotion/paths). L moves only between steps, over 40 f on E.rest per step pitch, and waits at each step for that step's work time from the data (machine-timed, 24-60 f). Draw the path twice: a 1.5 px C.line hairline for the whole route, and above it a 2 px C.ink stroke with pathLength 1 and strokeDashoffset = 1 - L / total, so the part already travelled is solid and the rest is a guide. Step row i appears on the frame the head reaches its y (pass_i): opacity prog(f, pass_i, pass_i + 12, E.smooth) with a 12 px rise through arrive(). While the head waits there, the row shows a dashed-ring spinner (one turn per 48 f) and TypeOn types its detail line at about 1.5 characters per frame. On the last frame of the wait (decided on fd), the spinner becomes a C.accent check that draws over 8 f on E.out, a 'Done' tag fades in over 8 f, and the head leaves on that same frame. Scroll the list container, not the camera, with a lagged follow written as a pure function: loop from the shot's first frame to f with c += (headY(i) - 0.4 x H - c) x 0.08, and add a 2 px/f drift, so the head sits near 40% of the frame height and the list never stops dead. At the corner the head turns first, and the horizontal follow inherits the lag as it carries the eye to the result at a constant 10-14 px/f.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Draw the head as a flat 10 px dot in C.ink (white on an ink stage) with no halo, bloom or blur. Mark its state with size instead (12 px while travelling, 10 px while waiting). The spine, the step states, the scroll follow and every timing stay the same. The full look relies on glow; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Head travel 40 f per step (E.rest), about 10 px/f for a 120 px pitch; wait 24-60 f per step, taken from the data. Row reveal 12 f (E.smooth) with a 12 px rise. Spinner one turn per 48 f; detail line ~1.5 chars/f; check 8 f (E.out); tag 8 f. Scroll lag 0.08 per frame plus a 2 px/f drift, peak about 12.5 px/f. Corner radius 40 px; horizontal run 10-14 px/f.
- **Use when:** An agent, build, deploy, import or onboarding process working through steps, where the point is visible progress toward one result.
- **Avoid when:** There are fewer than 3 steps (one status capsule says it), or the steps finish too fast to read (show the result with a count instead).

### Process-status pill with ring progress

`dn-status-pill-ring` · data and numbers · accent · energy calm · walkthrough, feature, launch

A compact capsule shows where a process stands in one glance: a live dot, a mono step label, a ring filled to the current percentage, the step count and a grey date.

- **Build:** Draw a rounded rect (radius 25% of its height) in C.ink2 with a 1.5 px C.line hairline border. Left to right, place an 8 px accent dot, a mono uppercase label (FONT.mono, 24 px at 1080p, tracking 0.15 em), an SVG ring (r 14 px, 3 px stroke, pathLength 1, strokeDasharray `${p} 1` over a C.line track), primary text at weight 500 ('Step 5/6 · Motion') and a C.mute date line. Animate it rather than parking it: the capsule rises 24 px on SPR.firm with opacity over 10 f on E.smooth; from the landing, the ring fills from 4/6 to 5/6 over 30 f on E.out, and the step digit rolls 4 to 5 through Roll on the fill's 50% frame. On the roll frame the dot pulses once, scale 1 + 0.4 * hitPulse(t, 2, 8).
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** The same capsule on a solid C.ink2 fill with a 1.5 px hairline border, no backdrop blur or frosted translucency, depth only from a soft drop shadow at about 0.16 alpha. Keep the live dot, the ring and the one step line ('Step 5/6 · Motion'); drop the tracked mono uppercase label and the grey date, which only decorate. The full look relies on glass, filler-text; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Arrival on SPR.firm (~24 f to settle). Ring fill 30 f on E.out. Step roll 14 f. Dot pulse: attack 2 f, tau 8 f. Visible 46-90 f.
- **Use when:** Proving that a real, structured process exists (pipeline, build, delivery) as an overlay on process footage.
- **Avoid when:** The step and percentage aren't true to the story; frames that already carry a headline, which the pill would compete with.

### Segmented tick gauge

`dv-tick-gauge` · data and numbers · accent · energy calm · any

Under a small label, a gauge of about 32 thin vertical ticks (3 px wide, 25 px tall) shows a value: most dark, the rest light.

- **Build:** Build: <TickGauge value on off> (fx/MicroUI): 32 ticks 3 px wide, 25 px tall, 3 px gaps; with at (and from) it fills one tick a frame. Anatomy: Ticks with 2-3 px gaps; filled share = the value. Sound: None.
- **Primitive:** `fx/MicroUI.TickGauge`
- **Timing:** Static, or a fill of 1 tick a frame.
- **Use when:** A percentage that should read at a glance.
- **Avoid when:** Animating every tick at once (fill left to right if it moves).

### Drag assets in, skeletons fill

`pd-drag-assets-skeleton-fill` · product demo · accent · energy medium · feature, walkthrough

The cursor drags a fanned stack of images into the input; after the drop they appear as grey skeleton thumbnails that fill with the real images one by one.

- **Build:** Build the stack as four image cards rotated −12°, −4°, 4° and 12° that travel with the cursor along cursorArc (src/fx/Cursor.tsx, bow 0.2) on E.smooth, each card evaluated 1 f behind the one above so the fan trails slightly; pressAt marks the pickup and the release. On the drop frame (or just after a cut), mount the thumbnails as C.mist rounded rects in the input's attachment row and fade each image up over 8 f on E.smooth with a 1.04 → 1 scale, i × 8 f apart. The input's other contents shift by FLIP as the row opens over 18 f on E.ui, and the drag path stays clear of any text being read.
- **Timing:** Drag ≈ 72 f on E.smooth; thumbnails 8 f each at a 6-10 f stagger (≈ 36 f for four); attachment row opens over 18 f on E.ui.
- **Use when:** The product takes real material as input (files, photos, documents) and the viewer should see that context going in.
- **Avoid when:** The input is text only; the drag path would cross text being read; more than six assets (show a count chip instead).

### Image resolves through representations

`dv-representation-cascade` · colour and light · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

An image is generated in front of the viewer: coloured dots pop into a grid with accelerating density, recolour toward the photo, then one frame of halftone, one frame of pixel mosaic, then the sharp photo; or a post image fills like a progressive render on twos (blank, a soft blob, rough shapes, final).

- **Build:** Build: <Cascade at src x y w h cols rows unlit palette> (fx/Cascade): round dots pop in power-in 2.3 over 38 f up to 58 % of the cells (each 1.4x large, settling in 4 f) in seeded palette tints (or vivid picture colours), recolour to the picture (14 f), then one beat each of halftone, mosaic and the photo (2.4 f each); ghost lets the empty grid carry the picture; the grid is sampled from src once (useImageGrid) or passed as grid; mode="progressive" loads blank, three fixed blur levels, sharp, on twos (46 f). Start it from a QuadLoader on the grid's centre cells. Anatomy: Dot fill power-in (0.6 -> 58 % coverage), recolour 6 f, final stages 1 f each; progressive stages on twos. Sound: A chat pop, a bubble pop, a cork pop on the reveal. Materials: The generated image grows from a speck to full width on twos while its content evolves like a diffusion render: pastel blobs (blur 12 px), then coloured clouds over dunes, then candy-coloured hills, then the final picture, each state about 6 f and sharper than the last.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cascade`
- **Materials:** The generated image grows from a speck to full width on twos while its content evolves like a diffusion render: pastel blobs (blur 12 px), then coloured clouds over dunes, then candy-coloured hills, then the final picture, each state about 6 f and sharper than the last.
- **Timing:** Fill 38 f, recolour 14 f, stages 2-3 f each at 60 fps; progressive 46 f.
- **Use when:** Image generation, rendering, any "it makes the picture" beat.
- **Avoid when:** Without a final image that rewards the wait.

### A shine passes through text while it loads

`dv-loading-shimmer` · micro-interactions · workhorse · energy calm · any

A soft band (about one word wide) sweeps left to right across a status line on every beat, turning the letters it covers white; a single word glows and returns to grey; skeleton cards pulse a diagonal shine twice; a textured shimmer passes over a filled prompt box before the press; an idle slider label shimmers letter by letter.

- **Build:** <LightSweep> clipped to the text, looped on the beat. Recipe until a primitive exists: background: linear-gradient(90deg, base 0 42%, band 48% 52%, base 58% 100%); background-size 250% 100%; background-clip text; background-position-x = 100 - ((f % period) / period) x 100 %. Anatomy: Band 150 px moving about 86 px/f near-linearly, then a rest; period = one beat (40 f, 90 BPM). Sound: The beat grid exactly. Materials: Anatomy of a type shimmer: the text is clipped to a gradient three times its width whose position slides one width per period. On a dark or tinted ground the band is white, about one word (5-7 letters) wide with 2.5 letters of feather each side, travelling about 0.7 letters/f and restarting at once (period about 40 f), with a slight bloom on the white letters. On a light UI invert it: a band darker than the grey base, about 40 % of the word wide, period 16-20 f; a dim band on near-white letters reads as a skeleton loader on type. Include the ellipsis in the sweep.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Exposure.LightSweep`
- **Materials:** Anatomy of a type shimmer: the text is clipped to a gradient three times its width whose position slides one width per period. On a dark or tinted ground the band is white, about one word (5-7 letters) wide with 2.5 letters of feather each side, travelling about 0.7 letters/f and restarting at once (period about 40 f), with a slight bloom on the white letters. On a light UI invert it: a band darker than the grey base, about 40 % of the word wide, period 16-20 f; a dim band on near-white letters reads as a skeleton loader on type. Include the ellipsis in the sweep.
- **Conditions:** gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
- **Timing:** Sweep 20-26 f; rest 18 f; pulses 22 + 20 f.
- **Use when:** Loading states; an idle call to action.
- **Avoid when:** Shimmer on headlines; glow halos.

### Spinner resolves to a check

`mi-spinner-to-check` · micro-interactions · workhorse · energy calm · feature, walkthrough, launch, vertical

A working indicator (a rotating dashed ring in a step list, or a small spinning disc pushed into the middle of a sentence) turns into a check with a short tag the moment the step is done.

- **Build:** Working: an SVG circle (r 10-12 px, 2.5 px stroke, dasharray '4 4' or a 270-degree arc) rotated (f - s) * 7.5 degrees, one turn per 48 f. Inline variant: open a slot between two words by tweening its width 0 to 1.4em over 6 f E.out (the words slide apart as flex siblings). In it, spin a 1.2em x 0.6em accent disc with a 3 px C.ink rim on rotateX, one turn per 24 f linear, in perspective 300px. Done: on the done frame (fd), replace the spinner with a check ring that draws strokeDashoffset 1 to 0 (pathLength 1) while scaling 0.6 to 1 over 8 f E.out. The tick path draws over 8 f from 3 f later, a small 'Done' tag rises 6 px and fades in over 8 f, and the step label mixes from C.mute to C.ink. Start the next step's spinner on that same frame, and put a pitched 'pop' on each check's 50% frame, climbing with each step.
- **Timing:** Ring: one turn per 48 f, linear (disc: one per 24 f). Slot opens over 6 f E.out. Check ring 8 f E.out from 0.6; tick draws over 8 f from +3 f; tag 8 f. One step every 24-36 f.
- **Use when:** The product works through steps on its own (an agent, a sync, an import), and each completion should land as a small lock.
- **Avoid when:** There is a single long wait with nothing resolving (show progress instead), or all the checks would resolve on one frame.

### Thinking indicator: icon, label and pulsing dots

`dv-thinking-indicator` · micro-interactions · workhorse · energy calm · any

A small status line says the product is working: an icon (a sparkle, a ring of circles, a face bubble), a word ("Thinking", "Searching") and three dots that pulse in turn (each darkening and growing about 1.4x, the wave passing left to right), sometimes with a token count.

- **Build:** Build: <ThinkingDots start size color> (fx/MicroUI) beside the icon and label: three dots darken and grow 1.4x in turn (20 f up, 20 f down, 25 f apart); ellipsis brings them on one by one first. Anatomy: Dot wave: each dot up 20 f + down 20 f, stagger 25 f at 60 fps (or a 12 f cycle); icon rises 14 f circ-out. Sound: None, or a soft tick per cycle. Materials: The assistant icon is a line drawing of a brilliant-cut gem (outer circle, eight kite facets, an octagon table) stroked with a vertical three-hue gradient, still, the only multi-hue element on a dark panel.
- **Primitive:** `fx/MicroUI.ThinkingDots`
- **Materials:** The assistant icon is a line drawing of a brilliant-cut gem (outer circle, eight kite facets, an octagon table) stroked with a vertical three-hue gradient, still, the only multi-hue element on a dark panel.
- **Conditions:** gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
- **Timing:** Cycle 24-60 f.
- **Use when:** Every wait in a product demo.
- **Avoid when:** Long waits (cut away after about one cycle).

### Brand mark rises alone and spins as the loader

`dv-mark-spin-loader` · micro-interactions · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

On black, the brand mark rises into place alone, sits for 5 frames, then words append beside it and the mark spins on its vertical axis as the loader.

- **Build:** Build: <Flip3D angle={spinAngle(f, start)} front={mark}> (fx/Flip): the mark turns on its vertical axis, a turn every 26 f, its back face hidden; Words appends the name beside it. Anatomy: Rise 123 px in 8 f; rotateY spin about 26 f per turn. Sound: A riser.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Flip.Flip3D`
- **Timing:** Rise 8 f; spin 26 f/turn.
- **Use when:** Product moments where the brand is the system.
- **Avoid when:** Spinning the wordmark.

### Corner handles turn on one after another: a loading chase

`dv-corner-chase-loader` · micro-interactions · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

The four corner handles of a selection turn dark in sequence (TL, then TR and BL, then BR) and back: a six-frame loading chase built from the frame itself.

- **Build:** Build: <Corners chase={{ at, color }}> (fx/Corners): the corners turn dark TL, then TR and BL, then BR and back, a step every 2.5 f (15 f a cycle; cycles to repeat). Anatomy: 2-3 f per corner; colour swap only. Sound: None needed.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Corners`
- **Timing:** 15 f at 60 fps per cycle.
- **Use when:** A selection or a card processing.
- **Avoid when:** Long chases (one or two cycles).

### Ellipsis dots arrive one by one

`dv-ellipsis-dots-arrive` · micro-interactions · accent · energy calm · any

The "..." after a status word arrives as three separate dots, accelerating (14 f, then 6-8 f gaps); a placeholder gains its dots one at a time while a more-button's dots resolve.

- **Build:** Build: <ThinkingDots ellipsis start> (fx/MicroUI): the dots cut on 14 f, then 7 f apart (22 f for three), then pulse; or HardStep visibility per dot. Anatomy: Dots cut on with shrinking gaps. Sound: None.
- **Primitive:** `fx/MicroUI.ThinkingDots`
- **Timing:** 22-24 f for three dots.
- **Use when:** Status lines and placeholders.
- **Avoid when:** All three at once.

### Progress line builds with counter-motion

`dv-progress-line-build` · micro-interactions · accent · energy calm · any

A dash becomes a line whose left end races left while the right end creeps; a short dash slides against the build direction under the bar; a coloured band scrolls once along the line.

- **Build:** Recipe: rect ends animated separately (left on E.snapOut, right slow); the counter dash a second rect. Anatomy: Width 42 -> 262 px cubic-out (peak 32 px/f at 20 %); counter-dash 13 -> 6 px/f. Sound: With the bar. Materials: A stepper advances as a 3D cursor passes under it: the next node goes from an empty ring (2 px, about 22 px) to a ring with a filled centre dot that scales in over 8 f, and the button dims to a pale tint over 16 f.
- **Materials:** A stepper advances as a 3D cursor passes under it: the next node goes from an empty ring (2 px, about 22 px) to a ring with a filled centre dot that scales in over 8 f, and the button dims to a pale tint over 16 f.
- **Timing:** 33-42 f.
- **Use when:** Progress, search bars forming, a line that becomes a field.
- **Avoid when:** A second multi-hue band in the same film.

### Status labels swap faster and faster

`dv-status-label-swaps` · micro-interactions · accent · energy medium · any

A status label fast-types (3-4 characters a frame), then swaps to the next; phrases change at shrinking intervals (15, 12, 18, 15, then 3, 3, 3, 3 f) before the cut, with giant cropped numbers beside them swapping too.

- **Build:** TypeOn kind="stream" per label with starts from an ACCEL list. Anatomy: TypeOn stream per label; HardStep swaps; intervals shrinking. Sound: A cut at the end.
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypeOn`
- **Timing:** Labels 16 f each; final swaps 6 f apart at 60 fps.
- **Use when:** Showing a process speeding to completion.
- **Avoid when:** Text the viewer must read.

### Grid loader of blocks: lit row steps, copies in phase

`dv-block-loader` · micro-interactions · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

A tiny grid of accent squares is the loader: one row lit at full strength with a dimmer trail row behind it steps down the block on drum onsets (irregular holds 7, 3, 1, 3, 1 f), the other rows step down to a faint level in four linear frames, the loader zooms in until its grid becomes the screen's grid, and tiled copies each run in their own phase so the field shimmers.

- **Build:** Build: <BlockLoader start x y steps={onsets} color> (fx/Loaders): 4 x 4 accent squares (22 px on a 46 px pitch), the lit row and a 38 % trail step down on the onsets (house holds 17.5, 7.5, 2.5, 7.5, 2.5 f), the rest steps down to 17 % in four frames; tiled copies take a seed (own 1-7 f schedule) or a phase; zoom={{ at, to }} pushes in until its grid is the screen's. The 2 x 2 version is <QuadLoader> (clockwise head at 100 / 38 / 17 %, a step every 7.26 f; tile(step) puts a picture in the head cell). Anatomy: 4 columns, cells 22 px on a 46 px pitch at the start; lit row 100 %, trail 38 %, others 17 %; zoom expo-in. Sound: A water-drop or sub hit at the start; row steps on kicks.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Loaders.BlockLoader`
- **Timing:** Zoom 18 f; row steps on onsets; dims 10 f in 4 steps; copies on their own 1-7 f schedules.
- **Use when:** Openers and loading moments in grid-based brands.
- **Avoid when:** Smooth fades between rows.

### Loader arc grows into a ring and the core swells

`dv-loader-arc-ring` · micro-interactions · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

Inside a screen a dot becomes a short dash, then an arc that grows 30, 60, 90, 160 deg, accelerating to about 300 deg, closes into a ring, and the dot at the centre swells into the hero button.

- **Build:** Build: <ArcLoader at r x y color core={{ to }}>{icon}</ArcLoader> (fx/Loaders): a dot (3 f), an arc growing to 300 deg on E.buildIn while it turns 6 deg/f (15 f), closing (4 f), and the core swelling into the button on E.snapOut (8 f): 30 f in all. Anatomy: Arc length on an accelerating curve while it rotates; ring closure; core swell. Sound: The beat (+7 ms) on the first frame.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Loaders.ArcLoader`
- **Timing:** Arc 0 -> 300 deg in 18 f; close + swell 10 f (30 f in all at 60 fps).
- **Use when:** The moment between a request and the result; turning a loader into the next object.
- **Avoid when:** A spinner that loops more than once before resolving.
